blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Sources for what’s nearby each building

items.t: East Newton is the Chimney Hill ground east of 144 Street, north of 64 Avenue and Hyland Creek, and south of Bear Creek.
It splits into three plan areas: East Newton North, East Newton South and East Newton Business Park, with the two residential plans split by 72 Avenue.
The Business Park sits east of 152 Street and north of 64 Avenue, and the Chimney Hill residential estate sits at the northeast.
This is a largely built-out planned suburb, not a town centre: the City describes the three plan areas as now largely built out.
Schools the City names in the area are Chimney Hill Elementary, T.E. Scott Elementary and Regent Christian Academy, alongside Valley View Cemetery.
Chimney Hill Elementary is at 14755 74 Avenue and T.E. Scott Elementary is at 7079 148 Street, per the British Columbia Ministry school list for Surrey School District 36 (SD36).

blocks.text: East Newton: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The local rule is plan currency: East Newton North was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP) update, and the South and Business Park designations were superseded by it, so the OCP now guides development.
A 2020 amendment removed the Business Park's live-work designation south of 66 Avenue and replaced it with business park designation, reinforcing employment-only use.

blocks.text: East Newton: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Chimney Hill is the local name and East Newton is the City planning name for the same area.
Valley View Cemetery sits inside the plan area, named by the City alongside the area's schools.
A new neighbourhood park, Woodward Hill Park at 6083 144 Street, is in planning and design on the City's park projects list, at the area's west edge.

blocks.text: East Newton: development and new projects

items.t: Full entry for this cluster: the City is widening 72 Avenue from 144 Street to 152 Street, the main east-west route through East Newton, as part of making 72 Avenue a continuous route from 120 Street to 196 Street.
The City lists no ongoing land-use plan for Newton, so no new neighbourhood plan is in progress for this area.
The local angle is the Business Park edge: homes do not mix into the employment block east of 152 Street, so no residential utility or tax fact is stated for that block here.
Newton Exchange, west of King George Boulevard, is the exchange for Newton, confirmed by TransLink as the terminus of the R1 King George Boulevard and R6 Scott Road RapidBus routes.
72 Avenue is the through-route, and the City plans it as a continuous route from 120 Street to 196 Street.
No SkyTrain station is in East Newton; the Surrey–Langley extension stations run on Fraser Highway, north of this area.

blocks.text: East Newton: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check lots on the north and south edges against creek requirements: Bear Creek bounds the area north and Hyland Creek bounds it south.
Do not rely on a rescinded or superseded NCP map for permitted use; the City states the OCP now leads development in all three plan areas.

faq.a: In Surrey's Newton community — the City describes East Newton as the neighbourhoods around Chimney Hill, east of 144 Street, north of 64 Avenue and Hyland Creek, and south of Bear Creek, planned through the East Newton North, East Newton South and East Newton Business Park NCPs.

faq.q: What plans govern East Newton now?
faq.a: The 1990s NCPs planned the subdivisions and the area is now largely built out, but the City states East Newton North was rescinded and East Newton South's and the Business Park's designations were superseded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update — read the current OCP and Zoning Bylaw, not just the old NCP documents.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in East Newton?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 110 houses listed with 16 sold in the month and 113 condos and townhomes listed with 20 sold in the month in East Newton. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is East Newton a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 15%, a balanced market; condos and townhomes had a sales ratio of 18%, a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.
